sourceUnits.title: Determination 2 左

sourceText.en: You like to eat the same thing over and over again until you try something new and if you like it, you switch to it. When choosing food, you should be guided by your taste, it should be tasty for you, it doesn’t matter if the food is healthy or not. Find what tastes good and what you like, you body will feel nourished and your brain will operate at full capacity. No matter how healthy the food you eat is, yu will never feel as good as when having something delicious. Try new things whenever you are in the mood to find what suits your taste. This is the most demanding type of digestive theme because sometimes you might end up not eating anything if for example it's not available somewhere you're travelling right now. Your selective body doesnt like to consume anything just because it's hungry. Sometimes it's better not to eat at all until you have a chance to eat a truly delicious food. Avoid eating things that you dont like for the sake of eating. This doesnt just apply to food. When you find something that suits your taste, you used only that thing, buying the same toothpaste, wearing the same type/brand of shoes, eating at the same restaurant, and so on. Overall, you should dispose of anything that's not to your taste. You are selective, but always ready to try out new products in order to find what you like. You are open to finding new things that suit your taste. You like to select products all by yourself, personally trying them out, and then sticking with the same product for a while until another one appeals to your taste.
sourceText.zhHans: 你喜欢一遍又一遍地吃同样的东西，直到你尝试新的东西，如果你喜欢它，你就会改用它。在选择食物时，你应该以你的口味为指导，它应该对你来说是美味的，食物是否健康并不重要。找到好吃的和你喜欢的东西，你的身体会感到营养，你的大脑会满负荷运转。不管你吃的食物多么健康，你永远不会像吃好吃的东西那样好。每当你有心情时，尝试新事物，找到适合你口味的东西。这是最苛刻的消化主题类型，因为有时你最终可能会不吃任何东西，例如，如果你现在旅行的某个地方没有它。你的选择性身体不喜欢仅仅因为饥饿而吃任何东西。有时最好不要吃东西，直到你有机会吃到真正美味的食物。避免为了吃东西而吃你不喜欢的东西。这不仅适用于食物。当你找到适合你口味的东西时，你只用那个东西，买同样的牙膏，穿同样类型/品牌的鞋子，在同一家餐厅吃饭，等等。总的来说，你应该丢掉任何不符合你口味的东西。你是有选择性的，但随时准备尝试新产品，以找到你喜欢的东西。您乐于寻找适合您口味的新事物。您喜欢自己选择产品，预先试用它们，然后坚持使用相同的产品一段时间，直到另一种产品吸引您的口味。

sourceText.en: Your type of digestion is sensitive to temperature. In an evolutionary sense, thisdiet represents the birth of the culinary arts and the use of energy for food preparation, human invented the kitchen and the ability to heat and cool food. You may not like dull or simply boring food, you need variety. You prefer sauces and gravies rather than eating dry food. The theme of your digestive system is 'thirst' and 'liquid'. You love something juicy and sophisticated. Thirst is not only liquids, but also a strong desire for something and you want it now and for the right food you will drive to the other end of the town. Your body is sensitive to temperature and fluids. Here, food acts as a regulator of your body temperature, the body regulates its own temperature by selecting drinks and food. sourceText.en: The phrase 'smelling things out' refers to the ability to perceive and detect subtle or hidden aspects of a situation or person, much like how our sense of smell can pick up scents that may not be immediately noticeable. This can apply to both literal smells, such as detecting an unpleasant odor in a room, as well as metaphorical or intuitive 'smells' such as sensing when someone is lying or when something is not quite right. Having smell cognition allows one to have a heightened sense of intuition and perception. it enables you to discern the truth from falsehoods, and to determine what is safe and unsafe. It can also help you to pick up on subtle energies or 'vibes' emanating from a person or space. The ability to smell thing out is not something that can be easily explained or taught; it is an innate sense that people with smell cognition possess. This sense can be further developed and improved through practices such as meditation, mindfulness, and tuning into one's own intuition in the now.
sourceText.zhHans: “闻到东西”一词是指感知和检测情况或人的微妙或隐藏方面的能力，就像我们的嗅觉如何闻到可能不会立即引起注意的气味一样。这既可以适用于字面上的气味，例如检测房间中的难闻气味，也可以适用于隐喻或直觉的“气味”，例如感觉到某人何时撒谎或何时不太对劲。拥有嗅觉认知可以使人拥有更高的直觉和感知力。它使你能够辨别真相和谎言，并确定什么是安全的，什么是不安全的。它还可以帮助您了解从人或空间散发出的微妙能量或“共鸣”。嗅出事物的能力不是可以轻易解释或教授的;这是嗅觉认知的人所拥有的一种与生俱来的感觉。这种感觉可以通过冥想、正念和调整自己的直觉等练习来进一步发展和改善。

sourceText.en: Having taste cognition can refer to both literal taste and an intuitive sense of aesthetic taste. You may have a heightened ability to discern what is considered good taste or bad taste in various aspects of life. When it comes to literal taste, one may have an enhanced sense of taste and may be able to detect subtle flavors and nuances in food. This may make them more selective or particular about what they eat, and they maybe able to identify when a dish is not quite right or needs some adjustment. On the other hand, the intuitive sense of taste may refer to an ability to recognize what is aesthetically pleasing or appropriate in various contexts. This may manifest as having a good sens eof style, being able to decorate a room in an aesthetically pleasing way, or having a knack for picking out the perfect gift for someone. Furthermore, the taste cognition may also extend to an enhanced intuition around language and communication. Having this cognition enables one to discern the nuances and subtleties of language and communication, allowing them to better understand and communicate with others. They may have an intuitive sense of what to say and when to say it, and may be able to pick up on the underlying meanings and intentions behind what others are saying.
sourceText.zhHans: 味觉认知既可以指字面上的味觉，也可以指直觉的审美味觉。在生活的各个方面，你可能会有更强的能力来辨别什么是好品味或坏品味。当谈到字面上的味道时，你可能会有增强的味觉，并且可以发现食物中的微妙味道和细微差别。这可能会使你对自己吃的东西更有选择性或讲究，你可能能够识别出什么时候菜不太对或需要一些调整。此外，味觉认知还可以扩展到对语言和交流的增强直觉。拥有这种认知能力使人们能够辨别语言和交流的细微差别和微妙之处，使他们能够更好地理解和与他人交流。他们可能对该说什么以及何时说有一种直觉，并且可能能够理解别人所说的话背后的潜在含义和意图。

sourceText.en: Outer vision cognition pertains to a heightened sensitivity to visual aesthetics. You may place great importance on the appearance of things, such as books, food, even people. You may be able to make quick judgements based on visual cues, and may be particularly discerning when it comes to what they choose to engage with or consume. For example, when it comes to books, someone with outer vision cognition maybe able to look at the cover and tell whether or not they are interested in reading it. Similarly, when it comes to food, they may be able to tell by its appearance whether or not they want to eat it. the meals have to be visually appealing. Additionally, this cognition may extend to the realm of interpersonal relationships. Someone with outer vision may be able to look at person and make a judgement about whether or not they want to get to know them. while it's important not to judge a person solely on their appearance, outervision may allow for a quick read on someone's personality, values, or interests based on visual cues.
sourceText.zhHans: 外视认知与对视觉美学的高度敏感有关。你可能非常重视事物的外观，比如书籍、食物，甚至人。您也许能够根据视觉线索做出快速判断，并且当涉及到你选择参与或消费的内容时，您可能特别挑剔。例如，当涉及到书籍时，你可能会查看封面并判断是否有兴趣阅读它。同样，当涉及到食物时，你可能能够通过它的外观来判断是否想吃它。饭菜必须具有视觉吸引力。此外，这种认知可能会延伸到人际关系领域。你可能能够看着人，并判断是否想了解他们。虽然不要仅仅根据外表来判断一个人很重要，但你能够根据视觉线索快速了解某人的个性、价值观或兴趣。

sourceText.en: Inner vision cognition refers to the ability to visualize things in the mind's eye and connect with one's higher self or intuition. This cognition can allow someone to tap into a rich inner world, full of creativity, imagination, and insight. Having inner vision one may be able to see things in their mind's eye with great clarity, and may be able to access their higher self or intuition with ease. this can be particularly helpful in times of uncertainty or when faced with difficult decisions, as it allows for a deeper level of insight and clarity.When someone with this cognition quiets their mind and steps into their inner world, they may be able to tap into a wellspring of inspiration and creativity. This inner world may be full of vivid images, symbols, and insights that can inform and guide their thoughts and actions in the outer world. overall, the gifts of inner vision can be a powerful tool for personal growth, creativity, and spiritual development. it can allow someone to connect with their intuition and higher self, and to access a deeper level of insight and understanding.
sourceText.zhHans: 内在视觉认知是指在头脑中想象事物并与高我或直觉联系起来的能力。这种认知可以让一个人进入一个丰富的内心世界，充满创造力、想象力和洞察力。有了内在的视野，你可能能够非常清晰地看到你脑海中的事物，并且可能能够轻松地跟你的高我沟通或透过直觉。这在不确定的时期或面临困难的决定时特别有用，因为它可以更深入地了解和清晰。当你安静下来并踏入你的内心世界时，你可能能够挖掘灵感和创造力的源泉。这个内心世界可能充满了生动的图像、符号和见解，可以告知和指导你在外部世界的思想和行动。总的来说，内在视野的恩赐可以成为个人成长、创造力和精神发展的有力工具。它可以让你的直觉和高我联系起来，并获得更深层次的洞察力和理解。

sourceText.en: The feeling cognition refers to a heightened sensitivity to the emotional and energetic qualities of people and places. having this cognition one maybe able to pick up on subtle energy and information that others might miss, and may have a keen sense of how a person or place ' feels' to them. It allows one to tap into the emotional and energetic states of those around them, thus when one encounters a person or places that makes them feel uncomfortable, they may instinctively know that they need to leave or distance themselves. This cognition can also be a powerful tool for connecting with others and empathizing with their experiences. however, it's important to remember that this can also be overwhelming at times, and that it may require boundaries and self-care to avoid becoming depleted or overwhelmed by the emotions of others
sourceText.zhHans: 感觉认知是指对人和地方的情感和能量品质的高度敏感。有了这种认知，你也许能够捕捉到其他人可能错过的微妙能量和信息，并且可能对一个人或一个地方的有敏锐的感觉。它使你能够利用周围人的情绪和精力充沛的状态，因此，当你遇到让你感到不舒服的人或地方时，你可能会本能地知道你需要离开或疏远他人。这种认知也可以成为与他人联系并同情他们的经历的有力工具。然而，重要的是要记住，这有时也可能让你不知所措，并且可能需要界限和自我照顾，以避免被他人的情绪耗尽或淹没。

sourceText.en: The touch cognition refers to a heightened sensitivity to tactile sensations and a tendency to use touch as a way of navigating through the world. Having this cognition one may rely on their sense of touch to understand whether a place or things to get a sense of what they have to offer. when someone with touch cognition touches a person or thing, they may be able to pick up on subtle energy and information that others might miss. This ability to 'feel into' the world around them can be valuable tool for understanding their environment. Additionally, one may have the ability to influence others through their touch. this could involve using touch as a way of providing comfort or support, or it could involve using touch to convey a particular message or intention.
sourceText.zhHans: 触觉认知是指对触觉的高度敏感，以及使用触觉作为浏览世界的一种方式的倾向。有了这种认知，你可能会依靠你的触觉来了解一个地方或事物，以了解你所能提供的东西。当具有触觉认知的你触摸一个人或事物时，你可能能够捕捉到其他人可能错过的微妙能量和信息。这种“感受”周围世界的能力可以成为了解你所处环境的宝贵工具。此外，你可能有能力通过触摸来影响他人。这可能涉及使用触摸作为提供安慰或支持的一种方式，或者可能涉及使用触摸来传达特定的信息或意图。

sourceText.en: This sense originates in the spleen and it's deeply rooted in our primitive instincts for self-preservation and survival. As individuals encounter others within their personal space, this sense is automatically engaged, assessing whether the interaction presents any potential threats or discomfort. Subconciously, the mind begins to evaluate factors such as the energy or vibe emanating from the people nearby, as well as their general behavious and demeanor. This assessment prompts the individual to consider their own feelings of security, asking questions like, '' Do there people make me feel secure?,'',''Is there fear or low vibration?'' and '' Are they trustworthy?''. The security sense is closely connected to the mind's desire for stability and certainty. The mind seeks reliable information, prefering clear-cut, black-and -white data to navigate its surroundings. In pursuit of a sense of safety, the mind generates strategies and plans to ensure that it remains secure and protected from any perceived threats.
sourceText.zhHans: 这种感觉起源于脾，它深深植根于我们自我保护和生存的原始本能。 当个人在个人空间内遇到其他人时，这种感觉会自动参与，评估互动是否会带来任何潜在的威胁或不适。 潜意识里，大脑开始评估附近人散发的能量或氛围等因素，以及他们的一般行为和举止。 这种评估促使你考虑自己的安全感，提出诸如“有人让我感到安全吗？”、“是否有恐惧或低振动？”以及“他们值得信赖吗？”等问题。 '。 安全感与心渴望稳定和确定性密切相关。 大脑寻求可靠的信息，更喜欢清晰的黑白数据来导航周围的环境。 为了追求安全感，你的大脑会制定策略和计划，以确保保持安全并免受任何感知到的威胁。

sourceText.en: As with the security sense, the uncertainty sense also originates in the Spleen center and is grounded in our primitive instincts for survival. This sense focuses on evaluating the trustworthiness and intentions of people entering one's personal space and aura. When encountering others, the uncertainty sense poses metaphorical questions to gauge the sincerity and genuineness of their words and actions. These questions include: ''what is the underlying tone of their speech?'' ''Is there something off-putting or untrustworthy in what they say?'' and '' Can i sense any hidden motives or intentions?''. This sense allow you to concern inconsistencies or unreliability in others, effectively ''tasting'' the authenticity of their communication. While the uncertainty sense may be open to engaging with others compared to security sense, it still maintains a level of caution and vigilance. Initially, you may not be entirely trusting or discrepancies or risks.
sourceText.zhHans: 与安全感一样，不确定性也起源于脾中枢，植根于我们原始的生存本能。这种感觉侧重于评估进入个人空间和光环的人的可信度和意图。当遇到他人时，不确定性会提出隐喻性问题，以衡量他们言行的诚意和真实性。这些问题包括：“他们演讲的基本语气是什么？“他们说的话有什么令人反感或不可信的地方吗？”和“我能感觉到任何隐藏的动机或意图吗？”。这种感觉使你能够关注他人的不一致或不可靠，有效地“品尝”他们沟通的真实性。虽然与安全感相比，不确定性感可能更容易与他人交往，但它仍然保持一定程度的谨慎和警惕。最初，您可能并不完全信任或存在差异或风险

sourceText.en: The third sense is now moving away from the spleen center and entering into Ajna/mind. This sense is linked to outer vision. It's very focused in what it sees in the environment and the people coming into your surroundings. It's about your eyes, what you see inothers, more than any other sense. When people enter your environment you think logically and practically. You are pushed to think about what needs to be done, what actions need to be taken so there is benefit for everyone. Because the sense is in the Ajna it also means you're the kind of people who needs mental stimulation, therefore the people around must stimulate you mentally in some way. But the most important thing is visual stimulation, looking at the others. Your mind is active, it is busy seeing those anomalies that break the patterns around you. Your mind can also get bored easily, sometimes wondering what to do.
sourceText.zhHans: 第三种感觉现在正在远离脾脏中心并进入眉心/头脑。 这种感觉与外部视觉有关。 它非常关注在环境中看到的东西以及进入您周围环境的人。 这是关于你的眼睛，你在别人身上看到的东西，而不是任何其他感官。 当人们进入你的环境时，你会进行逻辑和实际的思考。 你被迫思考需要做什么，需要采取什么行动，以便每个人都受益。 因为感觉在眉心，这也意味着你是那种需要精神刺激的人，所以周围的人必须以某种方式刺激你的精神。 但最重要的是视觉刺激，看别人。 你的思维很活跃，它忙着看到那些打破你周围模式的异常现象。 你的头脑也很容易感到无聊，有时不知道该做什么。

sourceText.en: This sense resides in the Ajna center, but moving to the right variable, so it's no longer linked to survival. This sense is all about a calm meditative mind as opposed to an active one. It also needs mental stimulation but required periods of rest so it can go back to revisit the experience. The way you absorb information is your passively, subconciously take it in during your experience storing it deep into your subconcious, then later you pull this informetion to reflect on the experience. In other words it is a relaxed mind, as opposed to an active, focused one. All if this means that you can find the truth already stored within yourself, close you eyes and meditate on it.
sourceText.zhHans: 这种感觉存在于逻辑中心，但移动到正确的变量，因此它不再与生存有关。这种感觉是关于平静的冥想心态，而不是积极的心态。它也需要精神刺激，但需要休息一段时间，这样它才能回去重新审视这种体验。你吸收信息的方式是你被动地、潜意识地在你的体验中吸收它，把它深深地存储在你的潜意识中，然后你拉出这个信息来反思这个体验。换句话说，它是一种放松的头脑，而不是一个积极、专注的头脑。如果这意味着你能找到已经储存在你内心的真理，那就闭上你的眼睛，冥想它。

sourceText.en: This sense is located far into right fixed territory and moving away from Ajna center into the Solar Plexus. To effectively utilize this sense, you need to tap into your feelings and carefully observe the behaviors and expressions of others. Those with a strong judgement sense posses a highly perceptive and discerning mind, capable of forming opinions and make decisions based on their emotional intuition. This sense is intrinsically linked to feelings of guilt, as well as the desire to rectify or modify situations based on one'judgements. However, this strong judgemental capability can impact your relationships and interactions. The mind's natural inclination to form opinions can evoke both positive and negative reactions from others, causing people to either appreciate or strongly dislike. The judgement sense relies heavily on drawing from past experiences with people, enabling the mind to form opinions and make assessments. This deep emotional and intuitice sense allows you to navigate the complexities of the emotional plane, fostering an awareness that can guide your interactions and decision-making processess.
sourceText.zhHans: 这种感觉位于右边固定区域的远处，并远离逻辑中心进入太阳神经丛。为了有效地利用这种感觉，你需要挖掘自己的感受，仔细观察他人的行为和表情。具有强烈判断力的人拥有高度的洞察力和雪亮敏锐的头脑，能够根据自己的情感直觉形成意见并做出决定。这种感觉与内疚感以及根据自己的判断纠正或修改情况的愿望有着内在的联系。然而，这种强大的判断能力会影响你的人际关系和互动。大脑形成意见的自然倾向可以引起他人的积极和消极反应，导致人们欣赏或强烈不喜欢。判断力很大程度上依赖于从过去与人打交道的经验中汲取经验，使大脑能够形成意见并做出评估。这种深刻的情感和直觉使你能够驾驭情感层面的复杂性，培养一种可以指导你的互动和决策过程的意识。

sourceText.en: This sense is situated within the right fixed territory and extends from the ajna center towards the solar plexus. To effectively harness this sense,you need to connect with your emotions and be mindful of the feelings and expressions of others. Those with a strong acceptance sense have a highly receptive and open-mindee nature, capable of embracing others based on their emotional intuition and understanding. This sense is intrinsically tied to feeling s of empathy, as well as the inclination to create an inclusive and accepting environment. However, this heightened sense of acceptance can also make you more vulnerable to being affected by the empotions and energy of those around you. The mind's innate ability to empathize and accept others can elicit a wide range of responses, leading people to either feel deeply connected to or detached from you.  The acceptance sense greatly depends on drawing from past experiences and interactions, allowing the mind to develop an understanding and appreciation of diverse perspectives and emotions. This proudly emotional and intuitive sense empowers you to skillfully traverse the intricacies of the emotional realm, cultivating a heightened awareness that can guide your relationships and decision-making processes.
sourceText.zhHans: 这种感觉位于正确的固定区域内，并从逻辑中心延伸到太阳神经丛。为了有效地利用这种感觉，你需要与你的情绪联系起来，并注意他人的感受和表达。你具有高度的接受和开放的天性，能够根据自己的情感直觉和理解来拥抱他人。这种感觉与同理心以及创造一个包容和接受环境的倾向有着内在的联系。然而，这种高度的接受感也会使你更容易受到周围人的情绪和能量的影响。大脑与生俱来的同情和接受他人的能力可以引起广泛的反应，导致人们要么与你有很深的联系，要么与你分离。接纳感很大程度上取决于从过去的经验和互动中汲取灵感，让大脑对不同的观点和情感产生理解和欣赏。这种引以为豪的情感和直觉使你能够巧妙地穿越情感领域的复杂性，培养一种可以指导你的人际关系和决策过程的高度意识。

sourceText.en: Survival - You have a primal need to see how you will survive (more self-directed view). Everything you do or not know is driven by fear, asking the questions ''How can I survive?''. Following your strategy and authoriy will get you out of the feeling of fear. Wanting/Need - You look at what the rest need or want. You get stuck in their needs and demands instead od you own survival.
sourceText.zhHans: 生存 - 你有一种原始的需求，看看你将如何生存（更自我导向的观点）。你所知道或不知道的一切都是由恐惧驱动的，问“我怎样才能生存？遵循你的策略和权威会让你摆脱恐惧的感觉。如果你在非我状态，就会出现想要/需要视角 - 你看看其他人需要或想要什么。你被困在他们的需求和要求中，而不是你自己的生存。

sourceText.en: Possibility - You see the possibility (coming from inspiration) in anything. You are a sampler, great for keeping up the spirit and can avoid all the sadness in life. You shouldn't turn things into expectation. If you are not in your self, it would be Probability - You say ' i know this' and bet your like on it. You are too rigid and close-minded. You see the practical probability instead of the possibility(comingfrom inspiration). This can cause worries, problems and kill your dreams.
sourceText.zhHans: 可能性——你在任何事物中都能看到可能性（来自灵感）。 你是一个采样者，非常适合保持高度精神，可以让你避免生活中所有的悲伤。 你不应该把事情变成期望。如果你在非我状态，就会出现概率视角——你说“我知道这个”，然后就押注在它上面。 这样你就太死板、太封闭了。 你看到的是实际的概率而不是可能性（来自灵感）。 这可能会引起担忧、问题并扼杀你的梦想。

sourceText.en: Power - You always seewinners and losers. You are here to keep score and let people know where they stand. With your perspective it's about the other(s) who has and who has not. You are the ones keeping track of things, like accountants and reporters, etc. If you are not in your self, it would be Personal - You dont care who wins or loses, who has and has not, Your focus way too much on yourself than the others.
sourceText.zhHans: 力量—你总是看到赢家和输家。 你来这里是为了记分并让人们知道他们的立场。 从你的角度来看，这是关于其他人有和没有的。 你是那些跟踪事情的人，比如会计师和记者等。如果你在非我状态，就会呈现个人视角分心——你不关心谁赢或输，谁得谁失，你比较关注自己多于其他人。

sourceText.en: Wanting/Need - You see what's lacking. You have a transpersonal view, looking out for the needs of the community. You see what is necessary and help people focus on that. Survival, you always fear about your personal survival instead of putthing the communit's survival first.
sourceText.zhHans: 想要/需要 - 你看到缺少什么。你有一个超个人的观点，关注社区的需求。你看到什么是必要的，并帮助人们专注于这一点。如果你在非我状态，就会呈现个人生存视角，你总是担心你个人的生存，而不是把社区的生存放在第一位。

sourceText.en: Probability  - You are here to have capacity to see what is going to happen. You are realistic, pragmatic, more focused and rigid. You always have assumptions of what is to be expected. Possibility - You see the possibility more than probability, saying 'That's possible...'' instead of seeing what's practically probable. You lack expectations.
sourceText.zhHans: 概率 - 你在这里有能力看到将要发生的事情。你是现实的，务实的，更专注和刻板的。你总是对预期的事情有假设。如果你在非我状态，就会呈现可能性视角 - 你看到的可能性多于概率，说“这是可能的......”而不是看到实际的可能性。你缺乏期望。

sourceText.en: Personal - You see the world through your own process which may appear selfish, seeing things that others cant. You are more disconnected from the world, having a unique view that can be perceived as weird and unconventional. If you are not in your self, it would be Power distraction - You are always measuring of competing, seeing winners and losers, keeping score, and are more connected to outcomes which barely affect you or having to do with you.
sourceText.zhHans: 个人—你通过自己的过程来看待世界，这可能显得自私，看到了别人看不到的东西。 你与世界更加脱节，拥有一种可能被视为怪异和非传统的独特观点。 如果你在非我状态，就会呈现力量视角分心——你总是在衡量竞争，看到赢家和输家，记分，并且更关注那些几乎不影响你或与你有关的结果。

sourceText.en: Fear - Fear as a personal motivation refers to the drive to understand, analyze, and navigate the world around oneself based on a heightened sense of alertness and awareness. You may have an innate ability to perceive potential threats or challenges, enabling you to take appropriate precautions and make informed decisions to ensure your survival and well-being. You often possesss strong analystical and problem-solving skills, which can be valuable in a variety of professions and situations. Your heightened sense of awareness can make you adapt at identifying risks, anticipating issues, and developing effetive strategies to address them. However, it is important for you to maintain a balances perspective and not allow your heightened awareness to become all-consuming or paralyzing. Excessive fear or anxiety can hinder personal growth and prevent you from fully experiencing life's opportunities and adventures. Need - Faced with the challenge of survival or achieving your goals, you may experience a sense of urgency that pushes you to take actions you believe to be essential, despite potential drawbacks or adverse consequences. This need-driven approach can lead to overlooking crucial details or alternative solution in unintended or undesirable way. It is essential to balance the drive for immediate action with thoughtful consideration of potential outcomes and risks.
sourceText.zhHans: 恐惧 - 恐惧作为一种个人动机，是指基于高度的警觉性和意识来理解、分析和驾驭自己周围世界的动力。您可能具有感知潜在威胁或挑战的天生能力，使您能够采取适当的预防措施并做出明智的决定，以确保您的生存和福祉。您通常拥有强大的分析和解决问题的能力，这在各种职业和情况下都很有价值。 你增强的意识可以使你适应识别风险、预测问题并制定有效的策略来解决这些问题。然而，对你来说，重要的是要保持平衡的观点，不要让你高度的意识变得无所不能或瘫痪。过度的恐惧或焦虑会阻碍个人成长，并阻止您充分体验生活中的机会和冒险。如果你在非我状态，就会呈现需求动机 - 面对生存或实现目标的挑战，您可能会体验到一种紧迫感，这种紧迫感促使您采取您认为必不可少的行动，尽管存在潜在的缺点或不利后果。这种以需求为导向的方法可能会导致以意外或不受欢迎的方式忽略关键细节或替代解决方案。必须在立即采取行动的动力与对潜在结果和风险的深思熟虑之间取得平衡。

sourceText.en: Hope - Hope as a personal motivation represents the drive to inspire and uplift others through one'innate intuition, foresight, or cognitive abilities. You often possess a unique perspective or insight that allows you to see possibilities and potential in situations where others may not. You are typically drawn to roles that enable you to share your vision and instill optimism in others. You may excel in fields such as teaching, coaching, counseling or spiritual guidance, where you can use your gifts to encourage and support others in their personal growth and development. However, it is crucial for you to remain grounded in reality and maintain a balance approachwhen sharing your insights. Over-idealizing situations or promising outcomes without considering potential challenges can lead to disappointment or disillusionment for both yourselves and those you are trying to inspire. Guilt - In the absence of optimism, you may experience a sense of guilt that compels you to take action and attempt to rectify situations. This emotional burden can lead to a constant drive for problem-solving and intervention, potentially resulting in overexertion, burnout, or neglecting your own well-being in the pursuit of ameliorating adverse circumstances.
sourceText.zhHans: 希望 - 希望作为一种个人动机，代表着通过与生俱来的直觉、远见或认知能力来激励和提升他人的动力。你通常拥有独特的视角或洞察力，让你在别人可能看不到的情况下看到可能性和潜力。你通常会被那些能够让你分享你的愿景并向他人灌输乐观情绪的角色所吸引。你可能在教学、教练、咨询或精神指导等领域表现出色，在这些领域，你可以利用你的天赋来鼓励和支持他人的个人成长和发展。但是，在分享您的见解时，保持立足于现实并保持平衡方法对您来说至关重要。过度理想化情况或有希望的结果而不考虑潜在的挑战，可能会导致你自己和你试图激励的人感到失望或幻灭。如果你在非我状态，就会呈现内疚动机 - 在缺乏乐观情绪的情况下，您可能会感到内疚，迫使您采取行动并试图纠正这种情况。这种情绪负担会导致不断解决问题和干预的动力，可能导致过度劳累、倦怠或忽视自己的幸福以寻求改善不利环境。

sourceText.en: Desire- Desire refers to the drive to acquire skills, knowledge, and influence in order to lead and inspire others effectively. You often feel a strong sense of purpose of guiding, mentoring and empowering those around you. Also, typically drawn to roles that allow you to develop your leadership abilities, such as management positions, teaching or coaching. You may also be inclined to engage in personal development and self-improvement activities to enhance your skills and expand your knowledge. However, it is important for you to be mindful of the intentions behind your pursuit of leadership. A genuine desire to support and uplift others should be the driving force, rather than a quest for power or control. Innocence, Due to a natural inclination to avoid assuming leadership roles, you may find yourself refraining from engaging in activities or pursuing opportunities that could potentially place you in positions of responsibility. This tendency could hinder your personal and professional growth, as it may limit your exposure to new experiences and the development of essential leadership skills.
sourceText.zhHans: 欲望- 欲望是指获得技能、知识和影响力的动力，以便有效地领导和激励他人。你经常有一种强烈的目标感，要指导、指导和授权你周围的人。此外，通常被能够让您发展领导能力的角色所吸引，例如管理职位、教学或教练。你也可能倾向于参与个人发展和自我提升活动，以提高你的技能和扩展你的知识。然而，对你来说，重要的是要注意你追求领导力背后的意图。支持和提升他人的真正愿望应该是驱动力，而不是对权力或控制的追求。如果你在非我状态，就会呈现纯真动机，由于避免担任领导角色的自然倾向，你可能会发现自己不参与可能使你处于责任地位的活动或寻求机会。这种趋势可能会阻碍您的个人和职业发展，因为它可能会限制您接触新经验和基本领导技能的发展。

sourceText.en: Need- Need as a personal motivation refers to a drive or self-preservation and security, often causing you to take action that you believe are necessary for survival. This motivation can sometimes lead to a narrow focus on fulfilling perceived necessities, even if it means overlooking details or potential consequences. People with Need as their motivation might prioritize meeting their basic needs, such as financial stability, physical safety, and emotional security, over other aspects of life. This can result in a tendency to be highly practical, resourceful, and adaptable in your approach to problem-solving. However, this stong focus on survival can also cause you to be overly cautious, inflexible, or unwilling to consider alternatives that may involve risk or uncertainty. It is important for you to develop balance between your drive for security and abiity to adapt to change or explore new opportunities. Fear - The tendency to reminate on hypothetical scenariosand potential risks, often referred o as 'what if thinking, can lead to excessive worry and an inability to make decisions or take action. Becoming consumed by these unproductive thoughts may detract from your ability to focus on the task at hand, hampering progress towards your obhectives.
sourceText.zhHans: 需要—作为个人动机的需要是指一种驱动力或自我保护和安全感，通常会促使您采取您认为生存所必需的行动。 这种动机有时会导致狭隘地关注于满足感知的必需品，即使这意味着忽视细节或潜在的后果。 以需求为动机的你可能会优先考虑满足基本需求，例如财务稳定、人身安全和情感安全，而不是生活的其他方面。 这可能会导致你在解决问题的方法上变得高度实用、足智多谋和适应性强。 然而，这种对生存的强烈关注也会导致你过于谨慎、缺乏灵活性或不愿意考虑可能涉及风险或不确定性的替代方案。 对您而言，在安全驱动力与适应变化或探索新机会的能力之间取得平衡非常重要。如果你在非我状态，就会呈现恐惧动机——反复思考假设情景和潜在风险的倾向，通常被称为“如果思考会怎样”，可能会导致过度担忧以及无法做出决定或采取行动。 被这些无益的想法所吞噬可能会降低您专注于手头任务的能力，从而阻碍您实现目标的进展。

sourceText.en: Guilt as personal motivation refers to the drive to make improvements or repairs in one's environment or relationships. Individuals with this motivation often feel a strong sense of responsibility to address issues they perceive as problems, believing it is their duty to find solutions and create balance. Guilt motivation can manifest in various ways, such as heling others, offering support, or solving practical problems. Those with Guilt as their primary motivation may also find themselves drawn to professions or roles where they can contribute possitively to the well-being of others or their community. While this motivation can lead to positive outcomes and strong connections with others, it is important for individuals with Guilt to ensure that they are notmotivated solely by an unhealthy need for validation or an inability to accept imperfection. It is essential to recognize when theirdesire to fix things is driven by genuine care and when it might be a manifestation of internal struggle with self-worth or feelings of inadequacy. Hope - while maintaining a hopeful outlook can be beneficial, it can become detrimental when it leads to passivity or an unwillingness to take responsibility for addressing issues at hand. Relying solely on the expectation that problems will resolve themselves or that others will step in to find solutions can contribute to stagnation, missed opportunities, and lack of personal
sourceText.zhHans: 作为个人动机的内疚是指改善或修复一个人的环境或关系的动力。 具有这种动机的人通常会对解决他们认为是问题的问题感到强烈的责任感，并相信找到解决方案并创造平衡是他们的责任。 内疚动机可以通过多种方式表现出来，例如帮助他人、提供支持或解决实际问题。 那些以内疚为主要动机的人也可能会发现自己被可以为他人或社区的福祉做出积极贡献的职业或角色所吸引。虽然这种动机可以带来积极的结果并与他人建立牢固的联系，但对于有内疚感的人来说，重要的是要确保他们的动机不仅仅是不健康的认可需求或无法接受不完美。 重要的是要认识到，他们解决问题的愿望何时是出于真正的关心，或者可能是自我价值或自卑感的内心斗争的表现。如果你在非我状态，就会呈现希望动机 - 保持乐观的前景可能是有益的，但当它导致消极或不愿承担解决手头问题的责任时，它可能会变得有害。 仅仅依赖于问题会自行解决或其他人会介入寻找解决方案的期望可能会导致停滞、错失机会和缺乏个人能力。

sourceText.en: Innocence - Innocence corresponds to the desire to experience life without predefined expectations or goals. This motivation is characterized by a natural curiosity and openness to explore the present moment without judgement or attachment. You are often more interested in simply being present and aware in each moment, rather than pursuing specific objectives or ambitions. You may have a talent for being objective observers, not easily swayed by your own biases or external influences. However, this lack of agenda and detachment from outcomes might not make you the most suitable candidates for leadership positions. Your strength lies in your ability to see things as you truly are, without being caught up in the need t control or manipulate circumstances. This can provide valuable insight and perspective, but it may no always translate into proactive decision-making or the ability to drive a team towards a common goal. Desire - While processing a strong desire to lead and drive change can be commendable, this passion may manifest itself negatively if it becomes excessive or overly aggressive. In your pursuit of leadership and your eagerness to ensure the success of your team or cause, you may resort to employing high-pressure tactics or unscrupulous methods. This approach can potentially alienate colleagues, compromise your integrity, and ultimately hinder the realization of your goal to make a positive impact on the world.
sourceText.zhHans: 纯真 - 纯真对应于在没有预定义的期望或目标的情况下体验生活的愿望。这种动机的特点是天生的好奇心和开放性，可以在没有判断或依恋的情况下探索当下。你通常更感兴趣的是简单地在每一刻都活在当下和意识到，而不是追求特定的目标或抱负。你可能有成为客观观察者的天赋，不容易被自己的偏见或外部影响所左右。然而，这种缺乏议程和对结果的疏离可能不会使你成为领导职位的最合适人选。你的力量在于你能够看到事物的真实面目，而不会陷入控制或操纵环境的需要。这可以提供有价值的见解和观点，但它可能并不总是转化为主动决策或推动团队实现共同目标的能力。如果你在非我状态，就会呈现欲望动机, 虽然处理领导和推动变革的强烈愿望是值得称赞的，但如果这种激情变得过度或过于激进，它可能会表现出负面情绪。在你追求领导力和渴望确保你的团队或事业成功的过程中，你可能会使用高压策略或不择手段的方法。这种方法可能会疏远同事，损害您的诚信，并最终阻碍您实现产生积极影响的目标

sourceText.en: Separatist - Someone who needs their space andit tapped into, as a resource
sourceText.zhHans: 独立主义 - 需要他们的空间并被利用为资源的人（偶尔被利用的个人）

sourceText.en: Communalist - A person who integrates with the community, independent, operating strategically for safety and security.
sourceText.zhHans: 公共主义 - 与社区融为一体的人，独立，为安全和保障而战略性地运作（努力分享你的天赋）

sourceText.en: Anti-Theist - Someone who is intuitive, existential, and 'Rejects God' - knowing they have a Divine Mind through self and others.
sourceText.zhHans: 无神论者 - 直觉的、存在主义的和“拒绝上帝”的人——知道他们通过自我和他人拥有神圣的思想。（在你内心寻找希望）

sourceText.en: A person who is 'looking for god' - knows something bigger is happening they can’t see, something outside themselves.
sourceText.zhHans: 有神论者 - 一个“寻找上帝”的人，知道一些他们看不见的更大的事情正在发生，一些他们自己之外的事情（从外部寻找希望的迹象）

sourceText.en: Leader - Someone who has the responsibility to lead, to take action and be strategic, and acquire the skills to do so.
sourceText.zhHans: 领导者 - 有责任领导、采取行动和制定战略，并获得这样做的技能的人。（带领他人朝着一个目标前进）

sourceText.en: Follower - A person who follows their own direction and what is right for themselves, instead of following someone else.
sourceText.zhHans: 追随者 - 遵循自己的方向和适合自己的人，而不是跟随别人。（引导自己朝着目标前进）

sourceText.en: Master- A person who's here to become a Master, to evolve from Novice.
sourceText.zhHans: 大师——一个来这里是为了成为大师、从新手进化而来的人。（逐渐精通某一特定领域）

sourceText.en: Novice - Someone who has mastered something in the past and wants to learn something new.
sourceText.zhHans: 新手 - 过去已经掌握某些东西并想要学习新东西的人。（不断地以各种方式从入门到精通）

sourceText.en: Conditioner - Someone who manipulates others by being strategic, conditions the rest and is more selfish.
sourceText.zhHans: 制约者——通过策略来操纵他人、制约其他人，属于自私的人。（为他人带来改变的催化剂）

sourceText.en: Conditioned - A person who is 'fixed', not impacted by the conditioner, but by global conciousness, and is more selfless.
sourceText.zhHans: 被制约者——一个“被固定”的人，不受制约者的影响，而是受整体意识的影响，比较无私。（不断完善自我去服务社会）

sourceText.en: Observer - A person here to be a watcher, detached and passive, a resource
sourceText.zhHans: 观察者 - 一个人在这里是一个观察者，超然和被动，一种资源（透过观察你的环境，你成为了一种资源）

sourceText.en: Observed- Someone who is an example and exemplifies something. A role-model
sourceText.zhHans: 观察到 - 以身作则并举例说明某事的人。榜样（你透过他人观察你作为榜样来影响他人）
